items.t: fallen to it — and it is that very thing. For I have declared plainly to you the hidden secret and the complete knowledge. May God make its reality firm upon us and upon you in the worlds, and may God spread out its path for us and for you in the two abodes; truly He is bounteous, generous. This, then, is the reality of the configuration of the spirits of duration (al-amadiyyāt), and of the realities of the things veiled within the lights of [divine] magnificence. /fol. 71r./ So be a believer in it and one who holds its realities to be true — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon you with a vast mercy, by His favour and His generosity; truly He is generous, compassionate, bounteous with all-encompassing beneficence. That is complete. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.
Chapter 12 (al-bāb al-thānī ʿashar): On the Greatest Name of God and the hidden operative deployments (taṣārīf) that belong to it[120]

Know — may God, exalted is He, grant me and you success in the knowledge of the Greatest Name of God — that in it there are momentous occult properties and indications. And we have already made [this] clear to you, so that you may see the secrets that are in it and the lights that God, exalted is He, has manifested within it, that its seeker may profit by it and understand its meanings and its wonders. And truly this Name heals from sicknesses and pains, and hastens well-being; and it is the impregnable fortress.

Among its occult properties: whoever writes it and places it in the grave of a dead man is secured from the punishment of the grave. And whoever carries it with him is in the keeping of God, exalted is He. And it is a mighty acceptance for whoever enters with it upon kings and the great sultans; and it protects him from them as one protects the sheep from the wolf. And the bearer of this Name is aided and given victory, and he subdues everyone who is hostile to him. And it is of benefit for the annulling of sorcery and for the loosing of the knotted spell, and for one whose imprisonment has been long; and it is of benefit for the epileptic (al-maṣrūʿ), and for the expulsion of the ghoul from the body. And if it is hung upon him — even should the possessing spirit (al-ʿāriḍ) be entrenched — that spirit is burnt away.

And whoever engraves the names whose mention is to come upon a signet-ring of silver, on the day of Friday, in the first hour — and let the engraver be fasting — and seals with it: no one's glance falls upon its bearer but that he loves him, and is gentle with him, and fulfils his need. And when he enters with it upon the sultan, he obtains from him his objects and his purposes. And whoever enters with it upon a sultan, let him stand at his right, and so likewise with all the rest of the rulers; and if he enters battle, then let the ring be on his left. And if that ring is placed in a ruined place, it is made to flourish. And if an unmarried woman carries it, she is married swiftly, by the leave of God, exalted is He, and suitors desire her — especially the virgin. And if one who fears highwaymen carries it — and whatever the matter may be — he is secured from what he fears and guards against. And if this Greatest Name is hung upon the standard, then that troop and that army will be given victory over its enemy, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And a certain king among the kings of the Muslims was besieging with it a city among the cities of the unbelievers for a period of seven years, until the Muslims built around that city another city — all this — and they were not able [to prevail] over that city. Then one of the king's intimates mentioned that in such-and-such a place there was a man known for asceticism and scrupulous piety and learning, and that he had become renowned. So he came to him. The man said: When he came to me, I received him with welcome and honour, and I asked him whether he had any need; and the king recounted to him what he had come on account of, and what the Muslims had endured from the siege of that city. Then the king said: Our desire of you is that you supply us with the blessed supplications. And when I heard the king's words and what he had come on account of, it became binding upon me to fulfil his need. So then /fol. 71v./ I took a slip of paper and drew upon it the noble Name, broken and spread out, and handed it to him, and I said to him: Set it at the front of your army and advance with the Muslims upon the city, for God, exalted is He, will give you victory over your enemy. So the king took it and returned to his army. And when it was morning, the king ordered the Muslims to advance upon the city, having set the noble wafq upon a banner in front of the army, as I had ordered him; and he advanced upon the unbelievers. And by God, it was but the blink of an eye until God gave victory to the Muslims and abased the unbelievers, and they took possession of the city and won a mighty spoil. And he sent to me a portion of the spoil, but I accepted nothing of it, and I said to them: Distribute it among the poor and the destitute — after I had enjoined that noble wafq upon them, and that they should guard it and not disclose it save to one who deserves it.

And among what has been mentioned of its occult properties also: that a man passed by Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr, and the caliph had summoned him in order to destroy him. And when that man saw him, his state having changed, he handed him a slip in which was this noble wafq. And when he entered upon the caliph, [the caliph] ordered the executioner to strike his neck. So he took the sword and meant to do what the caliph had ordered him; but his hand withered upon the sword. So the caliph ordered a second and a third, but the sword in his hand did not cut into the man. So the caliph said: Search him! And they searched him, and they found that slip with him, and in it was this noble wafq. So the caliph released him and ordered seven thousand dirhams for him; and the caliph commanded that this noble wafq be written out. And we have already mentioned a portion of its occult properties. And truly, whoever honours the verses of God, exalted is He, and His names — they honour him, and God, exalted is He, honours him with His supreme honour. And I mention also another counsel. I counsel you, O my brethren, O sons of wisdom, with this counsel concerning the Greatest Name of God: whoever knows it and works with it — by it he is among those for whom the caliphate was made obligatory after the successors of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace. And whoever God has favoured with this noble wafq, [let him] guard it from the base, and let him not deploy it in hateful things; and let his guarding of it be to the utmost of his ability; and let him anoint it with fragrant musk and camphor; and let him not carry it while in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), nor enter the privy [with it], if that be possible; and let him guard it from the ignorant and preserve it until the time of his need for it: he will find its blessing, if God, exalted is He, wills.

And whoever writes them and complies with the foolish, or gives it to one who does not deserve it — upon him be the curse of God, and of the angels, and of all people. For these seven letters were written upon the door of the Kaʿba, and they have angels standing in charge of them, charged with these names; and they serve them in the operation, and all that is in the revealed Books is from them, for they are exceedingly mighty. So if you wish to charge these spirits with a soul — as, for instance, to fetch your friend into your presence, or to turn back an enemy from you — then [know that] these names enter into seventy-two operations, /fol. 72r./ according to the number of the angels, every need having one charged with it: an angel from among those whom they bring before you. And these names enter into the bringing forth of things sought, and of treasures, and of buried hoards, and of hidden stores; and they have a mighty secret that is neither bounded nor numbered. So when you wish to work with them toward what we have mentioned, write them with saffron and rose-water and hang them upon the neck of a white cock, cleft-combed (afraq), muʿashshar, and release it in the place that is meant; and whatever place the cock halts at and scratches with its feet — and in one recension, that it crows — there will be the buried hoard and the hidden thing. And if you desire them for the demolition of fortresses and citadels and places, and their ruin, then seal with it upon the Seal of the operation of good, upon wax; and upon the other side seal with the Seal of the operation of evil; then bury it beneath the threshold of the door, and cast upon it some of the water that runs off from the bath-house. And if you desire them also for the driving of a man from town to town, then take a sparrow, a house-sparrow (dūrī), in the name of him whom you wish to drive off and to remove from town to town. If the operation is for a male, then let the sparrow be a male; and if the operation is for a female, then let the sparrow be a female. And you draw the signet on bird-parchment together with the name of the one for whom that is done and the name of his mother; then you tie it to the leg of the sparrow with a yellow thread, and release it with your left hand from behind your back; and you say at its release: So-and-so son of So-and-so has fled from this place in which he is, to a far place, by the right of these names. And they serve also for removal and transferral: you write the Seal of Evil on a sheet of paper, then wash it off with the water that runs off from the bath-house, and sprinkle it in whatever place — what we have mentioned will come to pass. And let that be at the beginning of the night, after the foot-traffic has ceased, in an inauspicious hour; and you say at the sprinkling of the water: O servant-spirits (khuddām) of these names, take charge of the removal or the transferral of So-and-so son of

So-and-so. So in the morning nothing was to be seen but their dwellings (Q 46:25) — and the like of this verse from what is in the Qurʾān. Come now! Haste! Speed! This very hour! And if you desire them for stoning, then write them on a piece of unfired potter's clay and bury it at the highest part of his house, and say along with it: And We rained down upon it stones of baked clay (Q 11:82) — the verse — and His saying: and He made them like chaff devoured (Q 105:5), and Sūrat Have you not seen how (Q 105:1) to its end; after you have suffumigated it with the incense of evil. You will see the wonder. And if you desire them for conflagration and the casting of fire into the house of a wrongdoer or of one who disbelieves in God — and it is not lawful for you to work it against a Muslim unless he deserve it, and the sin is upon your neck — then when you desire that, you take a white candle (shamʿa gharrāʾ), then you draw the name of the person and the name of the place, and you charge the servant-spirits with that; then you kindle the candle, and the fire does not reach the Name — and the names are those [already] mentioned — but that the fire takes effect in the house and in the garments of those named. And it is a perilous procedure: if you do not know its operative deployment in what we have mentioned, then the matter recoils upon you and you perish. And one of the gnostics worked it against a king who was a tyrant, unjust in his rule, and he perished, he and those who were with him. So understand. And if you wish to work with it for the disabling of ships from voyaging — and if they do voyage, they capsize — then when you desire that, write the signet in a wooden bowl /fol. 72v./ with the water that runs off from the bath-house and with the sea-water in which the ship lies; and take some of the water into your mouth and spray it upon the ship: it will disable its oars, and it will never sail again. And it is said that al-Maʾmūn, when he wished to take his diversion upon the Tigris, would draw the signet in its [proper] hour and hang it in the air, in a high place, by a thread of white silk; and God, exalted is He, would pour waves upon the sea from every side, until they were on the point of drowning; and they would know that this was from the operations of the caliph, and they would cry to him for help, and he would annul it for them. And if you desire them for the expulsion of the possessing spirit from the body, then seal with it upon the forehead of the afflicted, and recite over him the conjuration (ʿazīma): he will rise up, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you desire them for the deliverance of a prisoner, then draw the signet upon a little of the dust of the graveyards; then the prisoner brings it in through his collar and brings it out from his sleeve, and does the reverse of that after the recitation of the conjuration: the prisoner will be set free forthwith, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if you wish to work with it for the attraction of a human being, then draw the signet upon his footprint if that be possible, or draw it upon clean paper (kāghid) and suffumigate it with aẓfār al-jān (onycha), after you have written the name of the one sought and the name of his mother, and hang it in the wind: the one sought will come to you, even were he in chains. And if you desire them for the ruin of caravanserais and shops — and that is that you take kizza-wax, and draw the signet upon it, then you place the wax in the middle of a colocynth and write the conjuration upon its outside, then you bury it in the place: you will see a wonder. And if you wish to set the fever upon a wrongdoer, or a tyrant, or one who harms people, then do
— what I tell you.

And know, O seeker, that as for all the operations: if you hold fast, for their sake, to fasting, to ritual purity, to godfearing, to sparing of speech, and to refraining from acts of disobedience, then at that time, when you have drawn this seal and it is with you and you walk upon the water, your feet will not be wetted, by the leave of God, exalted is He, and by the blessing of this blessed seal, noble and mighty, which no one has ever known how to read in Arabic, save him for whom God, exalted is He, has willed it. Understand! For this seal has mighty occult properties, which we have abridged lest doubt come over the seeker so that he halt at their outward forms or at their meanings. And whoever has any portion of it apportioned to him — that is of the bounty of God, exalted is He. Have you not heard the saying of the Imām ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — that he said: the Qurʾān has an outward and an inward? And truly this blessed seal has an inward and an outward: its outward is what is seen, and its inward is the reading of it in Arabic.

And let us return to what we were about. And recall also another counsel — I counsel you with it, O brethren and sons of wisdom, this counsel concerning the Greatest Name of God: that whoever knows it and works with it according to its conditions is among those who have merited the caliphate after the successors of the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace. Truly this seal has seventy-two operative deployments and seventy-two angels, and that takes place on the eve of Friday after the last evening prayer; and they are servant-spirits (khuddām) from among the celestial and the terrestrial ones, so that you deploy them for your needs. And if you honour this Name, the servant-spirits will honour you, and everything you seek and everything you aim at will come right for you — and [you must] shun wine, and indecencies, and the eating of what is unlawful, /fol. 73r./ and treachery; and if you shun what I have mentioned to you, all your affairs will prosper. For when you have breathed upon a pot (qidr) while it is boiling, its boiling ceases. So know the worth (qadr) of these noble names, and guard them from the ignorant and from those unworthy of them. And if you wish to summon one who is absent, even from a month's journey away, draw the seal on a sheet of paper and write around it By the heaven and the night-comer (Q 86:1) in separated letters, and hang it toward the quarter of the person whom you desire and seek; and let your hanging of the sheet be in an hour agreeable to the Moon, and let the Moon be in an airy sign; and suffumigate, at the time of your operation, with the well-known incense of attraction (bakhūr al-jalb). Understand! And pronounce the aforementioned conjuration twenty-one times, and the person will come, even were he in chains and fetters. And if you want it for the ophthalmia of an enemy or an oppressor, take kizza-wax and shape from it a figure after the likeness of the one you intend, and draw upon it the seal together with the name of the target and the name of his mother; and put into the two eyes of the figure two thorns from the thorns of the sidr-tree, and put the figure into a black pot; and put into the pot unslaked lime, and sprinkle over it a little of the run-off water of the bath-house, and bury the pot near the stoke-hole of the fire. His eyes will become inflamed until he can look upon neither white nor black, and then he will cry out "Fire! Fire!" from the severity of the pain. And do not leave him thus more than seven days, for the one against whom it is done will go blind, and you will be the one held answerable for it on the Day of Resurrection. God! God! Do not perform this operation save upon one who deserves it. And if you wish to undo it, take out the figure, and pour the lime into the water, and draw the two thorns out of the eyes, and then destroy the figure or throw it into the water. And if you wish to disable a limb of a man, seal with the seal upon ʿazā-wax (mourning-candle wax) — and you shall have set the operation upon the name of the one you intend — and give it definite shape as a figure, and draw the seal upon it. Then draw the seal upon a knife whose haft is of it and in it, and strike the figure in whichever limb you wish, and that limb will be disabled from that very hour. And if you wish to deprive whomever you wish of sleep, shape a figure of ʿazā-wax, then draw the seal upon a knife whose haft is of it and in it, and upon it, and thrust the figure into the waistband of your drawers; and hang the drawers up, one leg above and one leg below. Then the one against whom it is done will never sleep so long as the drawers remain hung up.

And if you desire the harming of a person, and that grief, brooding, cares and sorrows should befall him, take a flask [made] upon the name of whomever you wish and the name of his mother; then draw his name and the name of his mother, and draw the seal upon it, after you have figured upon it the image of the target; and put into the flask a little sulphur, and something of pepper, and a little good oil, and set it over the fire between two graves. Then upon the one against whom it is done there will descend cares, and brooding, and diseases, and sicknesses. Understand! /fol. 73v./ And if you want it for love and affection, draw the seal in a glass bowl with musk-sukk, and saffron, and rose-water, and write the name of the target and the name of his mother. If you are able to give him some of that water to drink, he will never be able to part from you; and if you are not able to give him it to drink, sprinkle some of that water upon his clothes, and it will be just the same, and he will not be able to part from you for the blink of an eye. And if you want it for enmity, or for the uprooting of someone — that he be overturned from his place — or for separation between two persons, then draw the seal with musk, and onion-juice, and myrrh and botargo, upon unbaked clay; and pound the sherd and dissolve it with the run-off water of the bath-house, then pour it into the nostrils of a dead dog, and turn the dog over from its right side to its left side. And say, as you turn it over: "Turn so-and-so son of so-and-so away from so-and-so son of so-and-so, as this dog has been turned over, by the right of these names." And let what you write be the Seal of Evil, as I shall draw it for you. And if you desire reconciliation between a woman and her husband, seal the seal upon faraḥ-wax (wedding-candle wax) and shape from it two figures, and set their faces toward one another, and put into the mouth of each figure a piece of amber, and recite over them the conjuration twenty-one times, and let them be placed beneath the heads of the two of them. Then the two of them will love one another and be reconciled, and lasting affection will come to be between them. And if you desire awe [of yourself] among people, draw the seal with musk, and saffron, and sukk of musk, and rose-water; then wipe it off and keep it by you in a flask. And if you wish to gain admittance to one of the great men, take a little in your palm and anoint your face with it. Then everyone who sees you will stand in awe of you, and magnify you, and humble himself before you; and you will have great acceptance in the sight of every man.
And this is its figure — the Seal of Good and the Seal of Evil, as you see. Understand and ponder.
And this is its figure — the Seal of Evil, as you see.

And I have found in another copy, in an ancient book, that these names and letters are according to what I have drawn for you. The shaykh Muḥammad Qanbarīs, in the Ṣāliḥiyya of Damascus, said that he found this seal engraved in the Mosque of the Sufis upon the pulpit; and its figure is:

And this is the aforementioned conjuration by which all the operations are brought to completion, and it holds over the celestial and the terrestrial [spirits]. You say: Shamkhiyāl (×2), Shadkhiyāl (×2), Isrāfīl, Bakriyāl (×2), Sakhramiyāl (×2), Mīṭaṭrūn, Jibrīl — take charge, O servant-spirits of these blessed names, of such-and-such! — and you name whatever you wish of good or of evil from among what we have already mentioned. And these names exercise operative deployment in all the operations of this blessed seal of exalted worth. God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And know, O my brother — may God, exalted is He, grant us and you success in obeying Him and in understanding His secrets — that I have set down for you the ode of the Imām ʿAlī — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him and ennoble his face — which he composed upon the Greatest Name of God; and it is this blessed and renowned ode:
I began with "In the name of God" — by it my spirit was guided to the unveiling of secrets folded away within its inward.
Bāj Ahwaj, O my God, Muhawwajan; and O Jaljalūt, with the granting of the answer, Halhalat.
Pour forth from the lights an effusion shining upon me, and revive the deadness of my heart by Ḍayḍaghat.
That the life of the heart may be made clear of the defilement in it, by al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting), through whom the secret stood firm within it and shone forth.
5 Upon me [pour] a radiance from the lightning-flashes of His light — a radiance dawned upon my face and blazed.
And pour upon my heart the showers of mercy, by the wisdom of our Master the Generous, which has risen high over us.
Fayāyūh Fayāyūh, O best of creators, O best of fashioners, and most generous of all who have been described!
Bring me to bounty and to every object of need, by the right of the letters that are gathered together in the spelling.
By the secret of the letters that I have deposited in my conjuration, by the light of the splendour of the Name — and the spirit has risen high.
10 Pour forth from the lights an effusion shining upon me, and revive the deadness of my heart by Ghalmahat.
Come, clothe me in awe and in majesty, and hold back the hand of the enemies from me by Ṭayṭaghat.
Come, veil me from enemy and from envier, by the right of Shammākh Ashmakh Salamat Samat.
Come, accomplish my need by the light, O my Lord, and make my affairs easy after a hardship now ended.
And deliver me from every terror and hardship, by a wise text, decisive — the secret has been let down [as a veil].
15 And grant safety upon the sea, and give me the best of its land; and let down over me the covering, and heal [me] of error.
And bring the hearts of all the worlds, all of them, into love toward me, and grant me acceptance by Shalmahat.
And bless for us, O God, all that we gather of our earning, and loose the knots of hardship — Yāyūh — they have slackened.
Fayāyūh Yāyūh, O best of makers, O You from whose bounty our provisions have grown for us!
By You we drive back the enemies from every quarter, and by the Name we cast them upon the land in scattering.
20 You are my hope, O my God and my Master; so turn back the massed host, if it seeks against me some wrong.
O best of those petitioned, and most generous of those who give; O best of those hoped in by a community now passed away!
Kindle my star by the Name with light and splendour, for the length of the age and the days, O light of Jaljalat.
Yours are the bounty and the mighty power, for whoever comes to the door of Your court and takes refuge — the darkness has dissolved.
Bāj Awj Jalmahūt Jalāla Jalīl Jalā Jalyūt Ḥamā Tamahrajat.
25 Nayʿadādbarūm and Shamrāzāmaram, and Bahrat Tabrīz and Umm Tabarrakat.
/fol. 74v./ The lamp of lamps is kindled — a secret is its exposition; the lamp of lamps is kindled — a secret — it has been made luminous.
By the light of the majesty of Bādikh, and the veil of Naṭaḥ, and Quddūs Barakūt — by it the fire was quenched.
Biyāh Biyāyāh Namūh Aṣāliyā, by Ṭamṭām Mihrāsh — for us the enmity was warded off.
Bihāl Ahīl Shalaʿ Shalaʿat Shāliʿ, Ṭahī Ṭahīb Ṭayṭahūb Ṭaṭahṭīt.
30 Anūkh Batamlūkh and Banrūkh Barakhwā, by Tamlīkhiyāyāt Shamūkh Tashammakhat.
Letters belonging to Bahrām have risen and towered high, for the length of the age and of the times — Yāyūh — they have quaked.
And O Shamkhathā, O Shamkhatā, You are Shalmakhā; and O ʿAyṭalā — the downpour of the winds has been shaken loose.
By Ṭā-Hā, by Yā-Sīn, by Ṭā-Sīn — be for us, by Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm, [so that] felicity has drawn near.
By Kāf and Yāʾ, ʿAyn, Hāʾ and its Ṣād — our sufficiency against every terror that has encompassed us.
35 By Āhiyā Sharāhiyā Adūnāy Aṣbāʾūt, by Āl Shaddāy I have adjured, then Ṭayṭaghat [editor's gloss: "I conjure … against everything that threatens us."]
By qāf and nūn, then ḥā-mīm after them — or in Sūrat al-Dukhān there is a secret that has been made firm.
Three staves ranged in line after a seal, standing erect at their head like arrows.
And a mīm effaced, and one docked, then a ladder — and in the midst of it, like two jars, they are joined.
And after it four that mimic the fingertips, pointing toward good things — and provision they have gathered.
40 And a cleft hāʾ, then an arched wāw, like a cupper's tube, twisted out of the secret.
And the last of them, like the first ones, is a seal of five corners, and it has held the secret within it.
This, then, is the Name of God — majestic is His majesty — and His names have risen high among created beings.
This, then, is the Name of God: O ignorant one, hold it firmly, and do not doubt, lest the spirit be destroyed and worn away.
So take these noble names and hide them, for in them are secrets in which there is no twisting.
45 In them are the covenant, the compact, the promise, and the encounter; and truly with musk and camphor is it sealed.
And if he who bears them has fled away in fear, then come forward and do not dread the kings, by reason of what they contain.
And if he is one struck down, fallen upon by the jinn, then pour out scalding water: the body of the helper-spirit is severed.
So confront, and do not dread; litigate, and do not fear; and strive after provisions — you will be safe from error.
Four of them are from the end of the Torah, and four from the Gospel of Jesus son of Mary,
50 and five from the Qurʾān, and these are their completion — [reaching] to every creature, eloquent or dumb.
/fol. 75r./ No serpent will you fear, no scorpion will you see, and no lion will come at you with a growl.
Fear no sword, and fear no dagger; fear no wind, nor the evil of arrows.
O you who keep the Name whose worth is exalted, guard yourself by it against all things hateful and against harm.
And may my God bless, at morning and at evening, the Family and the Companions, by whose mention it is made complete.
55 I have sought access to You, O my Lord, by their standing, and by Your Most Beautiful Names when they are gathered.

And know that I have not mentioned the name of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — for several reasons. One of them is that the name of the Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — is a light, and were it mentioned in this place the light of these noble names would be extinguished, because his light — God bless him and grant him peace — is from the light of God, exalted is He. So understand that. And there is no harm if one of you, when he has recited these blessed names, seeks access through him to God, exalted is He, after the supplication; for his need will be fulfilled, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And the benefits lie in the convictions [that are held]. So understand.

Faṣl. And this too is the exposition of the names, beginning from his words: "Three staves ranged in line after a seal, standing erect at their head like the spear-point." These have an ordering that follows the ordering of the letters, and their ordering follows their non-Arabic (aʿjamī) form, just as he ordered it. He did not mention the Arabic letters, nor their Arabic utterance, nor [is it handed on] from breast to breast; and it is not set down in books except as you have seen, out of fear of the ignorant and of those who do not fear God, exalted is He. And here am I, making plain to you a portion of them, that you may infer their excellence and their blessing, and that they are spread out from three books: the Torah, the Gospel, and the Mighty Qurʾān. And as for their utterance in Arabic, no one has been gladdened by it; rather the gnostics receive it from their shaykhs, from breast to breast, lest it become a thing bandied about among the people of excellence — for it is the secret of God, exalted is He, [reserved] for the people of its unveiling. And whoever presumes to disclose a secret which his shaykh has charged him to keep hidden is chastised with what he deserves and is denied the benefit of that secret. As for what it contains from the Torah, it is six letters, and they are these: [Figure: the letter-signs as in the source — ]. And what it contains from the Gospel: [Figure: the letter-signs as in the source — ]. And what it contains from the Mighty Qurʾān: [Figure: the letter-signs as in the source — ]. So understand that, and conceal it, and beware of divulging it. Accept the counsel, and keep the injunction, and you will prosper by the help of God, exalted is He. And here am I, mentioning to you of its occult properties what it has been possible to expound and to mention, according to what my understanding has reached and my knowledge has compassed, and what I have been commanded to divulge, of the abstruse secrets it encompasses — before which the gnostics have halted, and from which those firmly grounded [in knowledge] have held back in reverence — just as their Master reported concerning them that they say: We believe; all is from our Lord — and none takes heed but those possessed of understanding (Q 3:7); and just as He reported concerning the noble angels, for all that they were given sight of the heavenly kingdom and of the earth, when they said: Glory be to You! We have no knowledge save what You have taught us; indeed You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise (Q 2:32). And God knows best. /fol. 75v./

Faṣl. As for his words, "and our seal after the three hastens on every affliction — entering the body, it sickens it": that is to say, if a man is afflicted with one of the inward diseases — such as colic (qawlanj), weakness of the liver, pain of the heart, and the like — and its remedy has wearied the physicians and its cure has baffled the sages, you draw the three staves and after them the seal, in this form which we have made clear, and it is as you see: [Figure: the three staves and the seal, as in the source — ] repeated 7 times. It is written in a vessel of glass, and set out under the stars for 3 nights, and given to drink to the sick man we have mentioned; and he is restored to health, by the leave of God, exalted is He.

Faṣl. As for his words, "hastening all the kinds of torment": that is to say, if someone has wronged you and you are unable to obtain redress from him, you draw the seal and the three staves and the spear-point (al-sinān). That is, you set up a figure of the fat-tail of a sheep in the name of whomever you wish and the name of his mother, and you draw the seal and the three staves and the spear-point upon every limb of that figure; and you will have laid that figure upon a board of the wood of the coffins of the dead, and you nail it fast upon that plank, and bury it near anāfī wa-huddadā [corrupt as printed; the parallel recipe names a place], or in a long khalʿ [readingkhalāʾ, an open waste, for the edition's .]Then the person against whom that is done suffers mighty distress, and whenever that figure melts, that person melts and his body wastes away. And should you write it for one who does not deserve it, you bear his sin and are among the wrongdoers, and you are the one held answerable for it on the Day of Resurrection. And God, exalted is He, knows best.

Faṣl. As for his words, "and a mīm for the coursing of the blood of every man who has waxed insolent": you draw a figure upon an unbaked potsherd, and write upon it the name of whomever you wish and the name of his mother, with al-ʿaynam ink, on the day of the two luminaries, while the two of them are in the [same] degree, before the separation. You write the mīm, and after it the three staves together with the spear-point, and the seal inverted; and you cast it into turbid water in a deep, disused well. From that very hour the need is accomplished, and the one against whom it is done does not cease to bleed from the orifices of his body until he perishes. So fear God, exalted is He, and consider for whom you write — you are the one held answerable for it.

Faṣl. As for his words, "a ladder by which you climb the steps of loftiness": that is that you write a ladder in its [own] shape, with no addition, upon the nail of your right thumb, and go in upon the tyrants in lawsuits and at the time of need. You will be granted victory over your adversaries in all circumstances, and you will be honoured, obeyed, your word accepted, your speech effective, brought near to their inmost thoughts, and they will fulfil all your needs. And if you write it on Khaṭāʾī paper and set it in faraḥ-wax, and it is placed under the tongue, he will not cease to be joyful and glad, of exalted station wherever he alights; their tongues will be knotted against him, and the tongue of every man of evil; and no contender's eye falls upon him but that he comes to love him, and everyone who sees him becomes expansive toward him and inclines toward him, by the leave of God, glorified and exalted.

Faṣl. As for his words, "and here are four, ranged in line for our battle": that is to say, the extraction of these four is from abjad, and their broken form (mukassar) is derived [from it]; and whoever breaks them and sets them upon a plate of /fol. 76r./ iron, and makes their number into a broken wafq (wafq mukassar), and carries it with him, and meets the enemy in the mêlée of war — no harm ever reaches him, even were he to fling himself among the spear-points and the arrows and the rest, and he is victorious over his enemy, the moon being in Daṭrūf Ḥasūs Radaf [corrupt as printed; an astrological position is expected]. And it is carried in a cap after one has fumigated it with such suffumigation of fragrant scents as is possible. Then he recites over it the Name that is in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, which is His word, exalted is He: Indeed your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne (Q 7:54), to the end of the verse; and he puts it on. He will then be secure in places of fear, and in the presence of tyrants and of those who do harm. So know that, and conceal it, for it is among the occult properties.

Faṣl. As for his words, "and by it the trees are called, and they come swiftly": that is to say, these four alifs, when their Arabic letters have been extracted, you draw [them] in the [proper] arrangement, on a night when the moon is in an airy sign, upon an unbaked potsherd, the moon in that sign being joined to Mercury in a conjunction of affection; and it is fumigated with the suffumigation known as "the gatherer of the spirits" (jāmiʿ al-arwāḥ), which is the one called among the masters of conjurations "the suffumigation of al-karājīm". Then he summons the person — and the man may be at a distance of some 15 days — while you recite over it Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together; indeed God is powerful over everything (Q 2:148); It was but a single cry, and behold, they were all arraigned before Us (Q 36:53); and He is powerful to gather them whenever He wills (Q 42:29). And you name that person by the name by which he is most commonly known, according to his repute; and he presents himself from that very hour. So ask him about what you desire, and seek his counsel about what you wish, and accomplish your need through him. And if you would like to return him to his place, repeat the suffumigation and recite over him this verse: and if it is said to you, "Go back", then go back (Q 24:28), to the end of the verse, and what is of like meaning in the Mighty Qurʾān. And you say: Return, So-and-so son of So-and-so, to your place in which you were and from which you presented yourself, by the power of Him whose command lies between the kāf and the nūn — His command, when He wills a thing, is only that He says to it "Be", and it is (Q 36:82) — to the end of the verse, to the end of the sura. And this is the meaning of "when we have accomplished the aim of a matter, we send it back".

Faṣl. As for his words, "and our seal, whose attributes were appointed for good": he means the last seal, which is the cleft hāʾ. When it is written, with the wāw after it repeated, it avails for the fulfilment of needs, the easing of affairs, the delivery of pregnant women, the binding of an adversary's tongue, the annulling of sorcery, the loosing of what has been knotted, the freeing of the captive, the release of the imprisoned, the attraction of provision, the increase of blessing in food, and the quelling of the rage of the overbearing man. It is written and carried, and you will see wonders of its blessing. And if it is written reversed — that is, with the wāw before the hāʾ and repeated, and after it 5 /fol. 76v./ cleft hāʾs — it becomes a bringer of anxieties, brooding thoughts, obsessive whispering, headache, terrifying dreams, and bleeding from the orifices of the body. And if you want it for the disabling of a livelihood, of a shop, of a woman held back from marriage, and of setting out upon a journey, be it by sea or by land, you draw it on a red sheet of paper and put it beneath something heavy, in the name of whomever you wish and the name of his mother — except in the case of the bleeding of blood. And you set the sheet down after fumigating it with myrrh, aloes, and asafoetida; and it is placed in a Persian reed, and a thread is wound about it.

— and you tie at the end of the thread a pellet of the hunters' lead, and it is buried in a water-channel that runs toward the east. Then the one against whom the operation is worked does not cease to bleed from all the orifices of his body until he perishes. And indeed [God] has willed the destruction [reading halāk; the edition prints hadaf and flags it as an uncertain reading] of the one against whom he writes it, when he deserves it, after three days. It is of the worlds of Mars; it works a mighty work in the shedding of blood and the destruction of souls. And God knows best.

Faṣl. As for his words, "that with it you may break all the armies and rout them" — that is, you extract this noble letter, resolve it into Arabic, and set it as a letter-based wafq upon the inner face of the tablet, on the 14th of the month, with the moon in a fixed sign, free of the malefics, and the sun in its direction, and the north ascending and not descending, and the ascendant in one of the signs that is the house of Jupiter. And when what I have mentioned to you has been completed, then that is the red sulphur and the greatest theriac. If anyone carries it in the midst of an army, he is given victory, and his enemy is routed and subdued. And its bearer remains ever within the safekeeping of God, exalted is He, and His care, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And if he carries it and speaks it, his heart is strengthened, and difficult matters are made light for him, and matters hasten to him however he seeks them, and he disposes freely in the world however he wishes, and then the angels obey him. And when he walks, the far distance is folded up for him, and the extremities of the earth are raised up for him, so that he sees what is far off as he sees what is near. And the spiritual beings address him and inform him of what was hidden from him of unseen matters. And he beholds, of the wonders of its blessing, what no measure can encompass and what neither foundation nor whispering thought can express. And among its occult properties: that you write a letter, or a slip, or whatever you wish, and it is folded and placed beneath his head; and he wakes [reading wa-yaṣḥū; the following word, printed nqyd, is unintelligible as it stands] to find its sides written over with whatever he desired — of denial or of affirmation, or of investiture with office or dismissal from it, or of giving, or of doing, of whatever kind it be, and from whatever person it be. And this is an utmost above which there is no utmost, and an end beyond which there is no end. So be sparing of it and a faithful keeper over it. And this is God's covenant with you concerning the guarding of it and the keeping of it concealed. And here I have made veiled allusion (talwīḥ) to you by the outermost fringes of allusion; and in indications there is what dispenses with [plain] words. And whoever fears God, He appoints for him a way out and provides for him from whence he does not reckon (Q 65:2–3). And God speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.

And here I set forth for you the names a second time, and their supplication /fol. 77r./ and their seal, which pertains to what we have mentioned to you. And it is this blessed and noble supplication. You say: O God, I ask You by the cloven hāʾ of Your mighty, greatest Name; and by the three staves that come after it; and by the arched alif; > and by the jīm <; and the mīm; and the effaced, docked one; and by the ladder; and by the four that are like a palm without a wrist; and by the cloven hāʾ and the magnified wāw — the form of Your noble, greatest Name. I ask You to bless our master Muḥammad by the number of every letter over which the pen has run, and to fulfil my need, which is such-and-such. And you name it, and make your intention good. And this is the form of the aforementioned wafq.

[Wafq: 7×7, cells as in the source — the seven cryptic signs of the Greatest Name named in the supplication above, arranged cyclically so that each sign falls once in every row and column; ] [Fig. 34]

And likewise, there follow upon this blessed and noble wafq seven letters of the alphabet, which are among the letters absent from the noble Fātiḥa (sawāqiṭal-Fātiḥa). To each letter of them belongs a name from among the names of God, exalted is He, following the aforementioned letters of the alphabet whose exposition is in the noble wafq. And they are as you see:
Fard (Single) Jabbār (Compeller) Shakūr (Most Thankful) Thābit (Firm) Ẓāhir (Manifest) Khabīr (All-Aware) Zakī (Pure)

Faṣl. If you wish to know the state of a sick man or of one absent, ascertain the day on which the sick man fell ill or on which the traveller set out, and reckon his name and his mother's name /fol. 77v./ by the greater jummal reckoning (al-jummal al-kabīr); and there is added to it what has elapsed of the Arabic month; and there is added to it the base (al-uss), 20. Then take the total of the whole number and cast it out by thirties — 30 by 30 — until there remains with you 30 or less. Then look at the remaining number and compare it against what I describe to you of the two tablets, which I have named the Tablet of Life and the Tablet of Death. And wherever the reckoning falls, judge by it, whether of death or of life; for you will see that, if God, exalted is He, wills. And likewise the case of a married couple — whether they will agree, or will separate, or whether one of them will die before the other: reckon the name of each one of them by the greater jummal, and add to the two of them what has elapsed of the Arabic month, and add to them the base, 20; then cast out and compare in the Tablet of Life and the Tablet of Death. If they are both in the Tablet of Life, they will come together and will not separate. And if they are in the Tablet of Death — or one of them — then either the one will part from the other or will die along with the other. And measure [the rest] by that. And likewise the case of two friends, and the case of two partners. And likewise, if you wish for the fulfilment of some need among needs, do with the whole of it as has gone before, after you have ascertained the day on which the partnership was contracted. So understand. And likewise the case of a governor at the time of his entry into a town: you ascertain the day on which he entered, and you reckon the governor's name, and add to it what has elapsed of the Arabic month, and the base, as we have set forth; and take what remains, and compare it against the two tablets, and judge by it according to what appears to you, whether of death or of life. And likewise the case of a pregnant woman and of what she will bear, and whether it will live or die in this birth. And it is that you reckon the woman's name, and her mother's name, and the name of the day you are in of that month; and there is added to it the base and what has elapsed of the Arabic month, as you have learned; and cast it out. If it falls in the Tablet of Life odd, the woman will bring forth a female; and if it falls even, the woman will bring forth a male; and if it falls in the Tablet of Death, the child will not live. And likewise the newborn: and for the [day] on which he was born there is likewise added to it the base and what has elapsed of the Arabic month, as we have mentioned; then cast out and compare. If it falls in the Tablet of Life, judge that he will live; and if it falls in the Tablet of Death, judge that he will not live. And likewise reckon for the victor and the vanquished, and for every perplexing matter. And God knows best. And this is the form of the two tablets, and they are as you see. So understand, and you will be rightly guided, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Fāʾida, called al-Qumquma al-Kubrā (the Greater Flask). It is of profit for every disease that is in the body. It is written on a sheet, dissolved in water, and drunk. And if you write it in a pure vessel and wash it off with a little sweet oil, and one who has some ailment among ailments is anointed with it, then God, exalted is He, removes it from him before long, if God, glorified and exalted, wills. And it is this, as you see. Understand, and you will be rightly guided. /fol. 78v./
[Talismanic figure (al-Qumquma al-Kubrā): five lines of cryptic sigil characters, as in the source — ] [Fig. 37]

Fāʾida, for the deliverance of a prisoner. And it is that the prisoner tread upon pure earth; then that earth is spread out upon a clean board of wood. Then write upon that earth the wafq that follows, in the first hour of Friday. Then let the prisoner carry it after praying two rakʿas, and he will be delivered swiftly, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And it has been tried many times over. And this is the threefold numerical wafq: [Fig. 38]

Fāʾida, from one of the masters — may God be pleased with him — of the people of divine oneness (tawḥīd). The master said: If you have a need [to be met] by God, exalted is He, and its fulfilment is slow in coming to you, then betake yourself to whichever mosque you wish of the mosques, and stand in its qibla, turning toward God, exalted is He, and say: O God, to You I have directed myself, and at Your door I have stood, and to Your court I have resorted, and of You I have asked; and through Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and the family of Muḥammad I have sought access to You; and through Your friends and Your chosen ones I have sought intercession. So fulfil, O God, my need, and relieve me of my distress. Then you name your need and what you desire. Then after that you pray two rakʿas, reciting in each rakʿa the Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1), Say: O you disbelievers (Q 109:1), and the two suras of taking refuge. And you say in the last prostration, while you are prostrate: And Job, when he called upon his Lord: "Harm has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful." So We answered him and removed the harm that was upon him, and We gave him back his family, and the like of them with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder to the worshippers (Q 21:83–84). Then you raise your head, and recite the taḥiyyāt, and give the salutation. And when you have finished the prayer, rise and stand facing the qibla and shake it [wa-huzzahā: corrupt; the feminine suffix has no possible antecedent and the sense is uncertain], and say: O God, Your knowledge has made me independent of speaking, and Your bounty has made me independent of asking. My God, as for the Arabs and the non-Arabs — when one seeking protection seeks protection with them, they grant him protection; and You are the God of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and I have sought protection with You, so grant me protection and do not send me back disappointed. And I have hoped from You for the answer, so answer me, and fulfil for me my need, and grant me my wish and what I ask of You, by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful. Then ask God, exalted is He, for your need, for God, exalted is He, answers your supplication by His favour and His generosity. And make the intention good, and beware of asking for what is not lawful for you, because the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said /fol. 79r./ ((Actions are only by intentions, and to every man belongs only what he intended.)) And by firm conviction you attain the thing sought. And God is the granter of success in what is right.

Fāʾida. It is said that within it is the Greatest Name of God. You say: O God, loosen this knot, and remove this hardship, and grant me to meet with the good of what is made easy, and guard me from the evil of what is decreed, and provide me with excellence in seeking, and suffice me against an evil outcome. O God, my plea is my need, and my provision is my destitution, and my means of access is the failing of my contrivance, and my intercessor is my tears, and my capital is my lack of stratagem, and my treasure is my incapacity. A drop from the seas of Your bounty makes me rich, and a mote from the flood of Your pardon suffices me. So provide for me, and have mercy on me, and grant me well-being, and pardon me, and fulfil my need, and relieve my distress, and dispel my worry and my grief, by Your mercy, O most merciful of the merciful. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace.

And likewise a fāʾida, from Ibn Masʿūd — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace: ((No worry and no grief has ever befallen anyone who then said: O God, I am Your servant and the son of Your handmaid; my forelock is in Your hand; what is in Your wisdom is carried out; what is in Your decree is just. I ask You, O God, by every name that is Yours, by which You have named Yourself, or which You have sent down in Your Book, or which You have taught to any one of Your creatures, or which You have kept to Yourself in the knowledge of the unseen that is with You —

that You make the Qurʾān the springtime of my heart, and the light of my breast, and the polishing of my sight, and my grief, and the departure of my grief and my worry and my complaint — but that God, exalted is He, takes away his grief and puts in its place joy. A man said: Messenger of God, shall one not learn them? He said: Yes indeed; it is fitting for whoever hears them to learn them, and that he not teach them to any of the foolish.)) So understand.
And I heard one of the righteous say, in a tried-and-tested supplication:
O God, make what You will in agreement with what we will, so that what I will may not become at variance with what You will.

They are translated here in their original reading order, recovered from the edition's own line-breaking, confirmed by the continuous syntax it yields at every seam, and independently confirmed against the parallel recension of the al-Ikhmīmī passage at fols. 41r–41v (chunks 025–026). So who am I, that I should will what is contrary to what God wills?
Though the servant strive and will, nothing has ever been save what He wills.
If what we will avails nothing, then be gentle with us in what You will.
And you do not will unless God, Lord of the worlds, wills (Q 81:29).

And know — may God grant me and you success in obedience to Him and in the understanding of the secrets of His names — that I have indeed seen people of ecstatic finding (wijdān) inscribing upon their hands, in the last hours of the night, this tenfold wafq (al-wafq al-muʿashshar) whose exposition follows, and asking God, exalted is He, by it and by His holy and noble names that are at the beginning of Sūrat al-Ḥadīd. And whoever likewise inscribes them in the aforementioned tenfold seal and hangs it upon himself — his supplication is accepted and answered, by the leave of God, exalted is He. And I saw in the noble Sanctuary a woman with her hair let down /fol. 79v./ and in her hand a tablet of gold with this tenfold [square] upon it, and she was saying: O Lord, O Lord, O Lord — by this, and by the noble names and mighty secrets that are within it, [I ask You] only that You bring me my provision without burden and without hardship; truly You are the Doer of what You will. And there came down a table from heaven, and upon it was much gold, and with it a written note in which was: "Had you asked God to carry you to your family, you would have come to them at this very hour, for you have called upon God, exalted is He, by His name which, when He is called upon by it, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives." And it is of benefit for everything. And God, exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way. And this is the form of the wafq alluded to.

/fol. 80r./

Dhū l-Nūn al-Miṣrī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — said: I saw a young man at the Kaʿba who multiplied bowing and prostration. And I drew near to him and said: You pray a great deal. He said: I am awaiting permission to depart. So I drew near to him, and I saw a slip of paper that had fallen upon him, written in it: "From the Mighty, the Forgiving, to My truthful servant: depart, forgiven what has gone before of your sin and what has come after." And Anas b. Mālik — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — transmitted that the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — passed by a man who was praying; and when he had finished the tashahhud he began to say: O God, I ask You, inasmuch as praise belongs to You — there is no god but You — O Ḥannān (the Tender), O Mannān (the Bounteous), O Badīʿ al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ (Wondrous Originator of the heavens and the earth), O al-Ḥayy (the Living), O al-Qayyūm (the Self-Subsisting). And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((Do you know with what he has supplicated? We said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: He has called upon God by His Greatest Name, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives. Ten names: al-Aḥad (the Unique), al-Wāḥid (the One), al-Ṣamad (the Eternal Refuge), al-Faʿʿāl mā yurīd (the Doer of what He wills), al-Samīʿ (the All-Hearing), al-Baṣīr (the All-Seeing), al-Qādir (the Powerful), al-Muqtadir (the Omnipotent), al-Qawī (the Strong), al-Qāʾim (the Upholder). There is nothing more excellent than working with them. And he said: they are of profit for the enduring of heavy burdens and of difficult matters.))

Fāʾida. This is the supplication of the names of which it is said that every name among them is the Greatest Name of God; and it is this. O God, I ask You, inasmuch as praise belongs to You — there is no god but You — O Ḥannān, O Mannān (5 times), O Badīʿ al-samāwāt wa-l-arḍ, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām (Possessor of Majesty and Honour), O al-Ḥayy, O al-Qayyūm, O al-Raḥmān (the All-Merciful), O al-Raḥīm (the Compassionate), O al-Aḥad, O al-Ṣamad, O Dhū l-Jalāl wa-l-Ikrām, O al-Wahhāb (the Bestower), O Khayr al-wārithīn (Best of inheritors), O al-Ghaffār (the All-Forgiving), O al-Qarīb (the Near), O al-Samīʿ, O al-ʿAlīm (the All-Knowing): there is no god but You; glory be to You; truly I was among the wrongdoers (Q 21:87). The Sublime Occult Properties of the Noble Name of the Essence (allah)
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. II, p. 3

The great scholars and saints of Islam are agreed that the Word of Majesty (Allah) is the Greatest Name (ism Aʿẓam). For the Word of Majesty is the noble Name of the Essence, while all other Names are but attributes of the Greatest Name. The noble Name of the Essence, however, can never be an attribute of any other name. If one asks, "Who is the All-Merciful (Raḥmān)?" the answer is "Allah." If one asks, "Who is the All-Forgiving (Ghaffar)?" the answer, again, is "Allah." The Word of Majesty occurs 2,360 times in the Noble Qur'an. For this reason, by virtue of the Exalted Essence, it is the most sublime of all Names.

Because the Word of Majesty is the sovereign Name that gathers within itself the beautiful meanings of all the other Names, it holds a sublime superiority over them. Since the qualities that each of the Beautiful Names (Asmāʾ'ul Husnā) possesses separately are all gathered together in the Word of Majesty, invoking it in remembrance (dhikr)

is equivalent to invoking all the Names at once. Remembrance of the Word of Majesty, made with any intention or purpose, is like a sharp sword. A person who turns to this Name of the Essence and prays with some wish in mind will see it come to pass even if he has been remiss in the proper conduct and conditions of prayer — for it is the pole and the greatest of all the other Names.

If the first letter of the Word of Majesty, the alif, is removed, it becomes "lillāh," which likewise points to the Divine Essence. If the second letter, the lam, is removed, it becomes "ilāh," which again is a reference to the Divine Presence. If both lam letters are removed, it becomes "Āhin," meaning "His Lordship." If one lam and the he are removed, it becomes "Ālin," which in the Syriac tongue means "God." If the two lam letters and the alif are removed, only the he remains, which is "Hū," a reference to the Divine Essence. But if a letter were removed from any other Name, its meaning would simply be destroyed.

To one who remembers the Word of Majesty by night and day, at every opportunity, the Truth Most High grants majesty, awe, and standing, and bestows exalted ranks upon him. He becomes accepted and respected among people. In truth, his understanding and the eye of his heart are opened, and he comes to grasp the secrets of truths that are difficult to comprehend. He beholds events before they occur.
[II 4] He forms a connection with the sublime spirits of the higher worlds and converses with them.
The noble Name Allah (c.c.) is the invocation of the Pole (kutub, the axial saint who heads the hierarchy of the spiritually elect) among the people of the Lordly circle.
1. Whoever lies down in his bed in a state of ritual purity (abdest)

and begins to invoke the noble Name Allah (c.c.), continuing the invocation until sleep overtakes him, will come to possess grace and favor and will attain the secrets of the malakut (the unseen angelic realm). He will behold auspicious things in his dreams. Every difficult matter of his will be resolved with ease. While he sleeps, no one can harm him, and no calamity or affliction will befall his household.

2. If the noble Name Allah (c.c.) is invoked many times over a patient before whom physicians have proven helpless, and if that patient's appointed hour has not yet come, he will certainly recover, by the leave of Allah Most High. Likewise, if a sick person himself invokes the Name Allah (c.c.) frequently at every opportunity, he will attain healing in the shortest time.

3. Whoever continues to recite the noble Name Allah (c.c.) with the vocative "Yā" (as "Yā Allah") one thousand times on Friday before the Friday prayer will see his provision (rizq) and earnings increase.
He will attain abundance and ease, and all that he wishes for will be readily fulfilled.

If a virgin girl wears this ring, she will make an auspicious marriage in the shortest time. Whoever possesses this ring should, at the very least, look each day at the Word of Majesty inscribed upon it and invoke the Name Allah sixty-six times. When one is about to make a request of someone, the ring should be worn on the right hand.

If this water is sprinkled over someone who has fallen unconscious in an epileptic seizure, the jinn afflicting the epileptic will be burned away, and by the leave of Allah Most High he will come to his senses.

Imam Ahmad ibn Ali al-Buni (r.a.) has said: I recommended this to a man who had suffered from epilepsy for thirty-four years. After fasting three days and observing seclusion (itikaf), he wrote the noble Name Allah sixty-six times on a plate and sprinkled its water over the epileptic. The sick man was healed and never suffered another seizure.

(In sense: "...that You fulfill the need of so-and-so son of so-and-so, at once, this very hour; and blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad, his family, and his companions.")
THE NOBLE NAMES HAY AND KAYYŪM (64th and 65th Names)

To attain every kind of wish and desire: keep a strict riyada and fast for 21 days. During the days of riyada, burn male frankincense (lubani zeker) as bakhūr, and eat foods such as raisins, dates, olives, and olive oil. At the end of the 21st day, draw the following blessed wafq of the noble names Hay and Kayyūm:

4×4 letter wafq of the divine name al-Wālī [Wālī], its four letters set once in each row and column — frame labelled with the four archangels: Gabriel [Jebrāil] top, Michael [Mikāil] left, ʿAzrāʾīl [Azrāil] right, Isrāfīl [Isrāfil] bottom. [II 49]

[II 49] Write Āyat al-Kursī (the Throne Verse) and Surat al-Hashr (the chapter of the Gathering) around the wafq, then take the wafq upon your person. On a green sheet of paper write the Āyat al-Kursī as well, and carry it with you. On the twenty-second day enter khalwa (a period of spiritual seclusion), and after every obligatory prayer recite the names Hay (the Living) and Kayyūm (the Self-Subsisting) one thousand times.

But make sure the twenty-second day falls on a Sunday in the second or third week of the Arabic month. When the fifth day of your retreat comes, a light will appear to you. This light will gradually gather itself into a person of pleasant and beautiful countenance, wearing a crown of light upon his head. He will greet you graciously; receive his greeting with courtesy and humility. He will say to you: "Why have you taken refuge in using this name?" You will say to him: "I wish to become your brother for the sake of God's pleasure." He will say to you: "Then I am a good brother to you" - and hold out his hand to you. Press your hand upon the green paper on which you wrote the Āyat al-Kursī, over the words "Allāhu lā ilāhe illā huwel hayyul kayyūm" (God - there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting), and hold it out to him. He will take hold of the paper at the words "Aliyyul azīm" (the Most High, the Tremendous). At that moment the pact between the two of you will be sealed. Say to him: "Give me a sign by which to summon you." He will give you a jewel, a ring, or a ring-stone. After you receive it, whenever you wish to call him, rub the object he gave you. At that moment he will come to you and you will see him in person. He will fulfil whatever needs you ask of him - except that he will not come at the time of the Friday prayer. Do not summon him at that hour!
